title: The real use case was not a planned top up

children.text: Virtual Accounts, bank transfers, and OTC already covered deliberate top ups. The gap appeared in a more spontaneous moment: a user needed balance while they were with someone who could fund it immediately.
In that situation, asking either person to look up, share, or retype an account identifier added friction to a task that should have felt instant.

callout: The Board request was simple: no number entry. The AstraPay user should be able to show a QR, have it scanned, and receive the top up.

title: Two cash-in moments needed different interaction models
description: The existing channels were not wrong. They were optimized for a different context.

left.label: Planned cash-in
left.title: Use account details
left.description: The user intentionally opens a bank, VA, or OTC channel and follows the required account or payment details.

right.label: Spontaneous cash-in
right.title: Show something scannable
right.description: The user is already with the person funding the balance. A displayed QR removes the need to exchange or type an identifier.
right.note: The interaction is built around proximity.

title: Reuse a QRIS behavior people already understood

children.text: The interaction borrowed a familiar merchant-presented QRIS pattern. Instead of teaching a new transfer behavior, AstraPay generates a QR that the funding person can scan.
The direction of money changes, but the visible behavior stays familiar: present QR, scan, pay, confirm.

callout: The design reduced learning by reusing an existing payment habit rather than inventing a new cash-in ritual.

alt: QRIS Top Up concept showing a displayed QR used for cash-in

title: Six moments were enough for the visible journey

children.text: Open Top Up, choose QRIS, enter the amount, display the QR, let the funding person scan and pay, then update the top-up status.
The screens stay simple because most of the complexity belongs to transaction handling rather than navigation.

title: Inspect the QRIS Top Up flow
The hard part started after the QR appeared

children.text: Generating a QR is only the beginning of a money movement flow. The interface also has to distinguish a bill that is waiting, paid, expired, or temporarily unresolved.

I worked with engineering so the status shown to users followed the transaction state in the backend. The product should never celebrate a successful top up while the system still considers the bill unresolved.

callout: For a transaction product, the UI state is only trustworthy when it is tied to the same source of truth as the payment state.

title: Add the transaction-state diagram here

children.text: Replace this block with the simplified system flow once the asset is ready.

The useful version should show QR or bill creation, waiting for payment, callback or status checking, paid and balance updated, expiry, and the retry or temporary-error branch. Keep it at product-system level rather than exposing implementation details that should stay internal.

callout: Asset needed: a simplified state diagram from QR generated to paid, expired, or temporary failure.

title: The product had to work on two layers at once
description: The visible flow stayed short while the system underneath protected transaction correctness.

left.label: User-facing
left.title: Make the state obvious
left.description: Generate the QR, show what is waiting, confirm payment, and communicate expiry or a recoverable issue without making users interpret backend terminology.
left.note: Clarity at the moment of payment.

right.label: System-facing
right.title: Keep the transaction safe
right.description: Create bill, status checks, callbacks, retries, and idempotency have to resolve into one reliable product state.

title: Designing the interface meant understanding the transaction sequence

children.text: Idempotency
Repeated requests should not create duplicate transactions.
Retry policy
Temporary failures need a controlled recovery path without creating repeated uncontrolled requests.
Observability
Logs and metrics need to make production issues traceable when a payment state does not resolve as expected.
Transaction sequence
Create bill, bill status, and callback notifications need to converge before the interface communicates the final state.

callout: The interaction only stays credible when product, frontend, backend, and payment-state behavior agree on what happened.

title: Add the adoption curve when the raw data is ready

children.text: The current evidence proves scale at one point in time, but it does not show how adoption developed.

If monthly data is available, add a trend from launch through 2026 using either QRIS Top Up share or successful transaction volume. A second useful view would be the operational funnel from QR created to scanned or paid, including expiry and failure rates.

callout: Data needed: monthly channel share or transaction volume, QR-created to paid conversion, expiry rate, and failure or delayed-callback rate.

title: The simplest interaction came from using a model that already existed

children.text: The feature did not need a new payment language. It needed the right existing behavior applied to a different cash-in moment.
The visible flow could stay small because the design work also covered the transaction states behind it. That combination mattered more than adding more screens.
